source.citation: E. M. Rosen, VMGSim: Revisiting the Cavett Problem, CACHE News Fall (2005)
source.access: Open access: free to read on the website of CACHE (Computer Aids for Chemical Engineering Education)
source.tables: Figure 2 (VMGSim flowsheet of the Cavett problem: units, streams, recycles R1, R2, R3) and Figure 3 (fixed pressures and temperatures of FL1-FL4, feed temperature, pressure and flows, products P1 and P2 of VMGSim with advanced Peng-Robinson and of FLOWTRAN as given by Rosen and Pauls, 1977). Values copied as printed; the PDF's text was extracted and checked against the page image.

units: flows in mol/hr as printed (lb-mol/hr in the original problem); pressures psia; temperatures degrees F
notes: FLOWTRAN's P1 ethane, 2883.2, is above the feed (2395.5); Rosen reads it as a typo for 2383.2. FLOWTRAN's products do not close the component balances (Rosen's last column); VMGSim's do. P1 is the vapour of FL1, P2 the liquid of FL4 (Figure 2). Rosen's text says P2 is the liquid of FL2; Figure 2 and the stated conditions (85 F, 13 psia) are those of FL4.
